rv.q: This fun, witty production, with its sumptuous sets, highlights the British obsession with class and taste, but it overlooks Shaw’s subtler and less comfortable truths.
But Prowse's production seems more concerned with effects than ideas.
This is Professor Higgins as Jack the Ripper.

Their big showdown, played facing each other while seated on the red banquettes that are endemic to Prowse’s “theatrical” setting of red swags, false prosceniums and mottled pillars, is as electrifying as any version of that scene I can recall.
But before that, there’s a lot of sexist rubbish to be endured.

cn.t: Shaw's classic receives a respectable but uneven revival, with Kara Tointon's luminous West End debut as Eliza earning praise alongside Philip Prowse's striking design, though some find the production coarse and overstated.
